companyRankingLists.itemDescription: It’s year 27 on the list for this grocery retailer, which operates in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Virginia—and this year opened operations in Kentucky. The company is over 90 years old and currently operates more than 1,365 grocery stores, 370 liquor stores, and 14 stand-alone pharmacies. Its success seems to start in the company culture—new hires are oriented by Publix cultural ambassadors, who range from age 19 to 72, on their first day. It also helps associates volunteer at state parks through their two annual environmental weeks. Last spring, over 6,200 employees volunteered at hundreds of state parks, gardens, and zoos to clean up waterways, remove invasive plants, and complete repairs. In September, just under 6,300 associates volunteered to help people facing food insecurity. The company also expanded its paid parental leave policy to allow anyone who has welcomed a new child in their lives an option for paid time off during the first year following birth or adoption.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
This grocery retailer operating in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Virginia has been on the Best Companies to Work For list for 26 years.

  • Association Appreciate Visits give store associates the chance to directly meet, engage with, and ask questions of senior management.

  • Eligible employees can become company owners in one of three ways: through 401(k) contributions, purchasing stock, and the employee stock ownership plan.

  • Full- and part-time associates working an average of 10 hours per week can access some tuition reimbursement in approved fields and for associate degrees or GEDs.

  • Publix partners with Urban League affiliates to provide career development courses for associates.

  • No Publix has ever conducted a layoff.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The 1,341-store supermarket chain Publix is the largest employee-owned company in the U.S., meaning its stock isn’t publicly traded and is only available to its 240,000-plus employees and board members. It dropped nine spots on this year’s Fortune 500.

  • The grocer continued its healthy top-line performance with $55 billion in 2022 revenues, a 13.5% increase over 2021.

  • Publix’s 33.9% decline in net earnings to $2.9 billion in 2022 was almost entirely driven by $1.3 billion in investment losses.

  • By the end of 2023, Publix will open its first store in Kentucky (with a further three planned), marking its expansion into an eighth U.S. state.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The 91-year-old regional grocery chain based in Lakeland, Fla., generated $48 billion in revenue last year, making it the largest employee-owned company in the U.S. Only current employees and board directors can purchase Publix stock, which has turned many longtime staffers into millionaires. CEO Todd Jones, who himself started as a bagger, says the model is part of the company’s secret sauce: Employees feel like they have skin in the game. Staff at Publix tend to stick around, and many see career growth; some 90% of store managers started out working on the floor. Read more: Shoppers are obsessed with Publix and Wegmans. Here’s what it’s really like to work there.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Publix Super Markets, founded in 1930, is the largest employee-owned company in the U.S. During the pandemic, the culture around employee ownership has helped Publix to retain employees and keep operations steady at a time when many other grocers have grappled with high turnover. In April 2022, the company's board of directors approved a five-for-one stock split that lowered the price of shares and made it easier for newer employees to buy in. The chain has almost 1,300 stores, primarily in the southeastern U.S., and Publix saw a 7% increase in revenue in 2021. Publix also recently donated more than 50 million pounds of produce as part of an initiative to support farmers and food banks in the Southeast.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Like other grocers, Publix thrived during the pandemic as people increasingly cooked at home and consolidated shopping at fewer places. The 1,264-store Florida-based chain took a number of steps to safeguard its workers’ well-being. Publix added mental health care to its benefits, paid for employees’ coronavirus treatment, and compensated workers who were exposed to the virus and had to quarantine. Publix also launched an initiative to source more produce and milk locally, donating these supplies to anti-hunger groups.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The 1,266-store chain, dominant in the Southern U.S., held on to its crown in 2020 as the world’s largest worker-owned business. Like its grocery peers, Publix’s top-line results soared under lockdown, notching a record $44.9 billion in sales—a 17.7% increase from 2019. Gross earnings too climbed by $1 billion from the year-earlier period. The company enters 2021 in a position of strength. It has already opened 39 new supermarkets and is remodeling another 154 stores. And with its stores serving as COVID-19 vaccination distribution points, Publix expects foot traffic to be strong again this year.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The Lakeland, Fla. company is owned by its 200,000 employees, making it the world’s largest worker-owned business. Operating more than 1,200 supermarkets throughout the southeastern U.S., Publix is one of the best-performing companies in the grocery sector. In 2019, overall sales increased 5.6% year-on-year, and the company maintained an operating profit margin of 7.6%—both figures more than double the industry average. The chain invested more than $1 billion in expansion in 2019, opening 35 new stores, and remodeling 177 others, as well as acquiring shopping centers in which its supermarkets were the anchor tenants. It announced plans to further ramp up capital spending in 2020, committing $1.6 billion to similar investments.

"I feel as though Publix still believes in the American Dream as George Jenkins would have wanted. My store manager started as a cashier, I began with my first high school job as a bagger 8 years ago and now I plan on retiring with the company-the possibilities here are endless. We started from humble beginnings and we have not compromised that for the sake of growth. We take care of employees with benefits like I have never seen before this. I began my yolk at 18 years old thanks to Publix. My favorite thing about Publix though: our desire to be better-to seek improvement and be open to change. The associate has a voice at Publix — and that makes me feel valued as a person," says one millennial associate.

 

According to another millennial, "Publix has a lot of opportunities for advancement. I think it's great that they only promote within the company giving anyone a fair chance at building a career with the company no matter what your schooling background is or where you've previously have worked."

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
